record.paper_title: Open Problems Related to Algebraic Attacks on Stream Ciphers
record.original_question: For a multi-output Boolean function, and in particular for augmented functions whose Boolean output components are all linearly equivalent, does that linear equivalence among the output components affect the algebraic immunity of the multi-output function?

evidence.quote: For instance, a very particular property of the augmented function is that all its Boolean components are lin￾early equivalent.
Open problem 8. Does the linear equivalence between all output components of a multi-output function influence its algebraic immunity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F:\mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2^m$ be a multi-output Boolean function with coordinate functions $f_1,\dots,f_m:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$. Two Boolean functions $g,h:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ are called linearly equivalent if there exists an invertible linear map $L\in GL_n(\mathbb{F}_2)$ such that $h(x)=g(Lx)$ for all $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The algebraic immunity of $F$, denoted $\mathrm{AI}(F)$, is defined as the minimum algebraic degree of a nonzero Boolean function $g:\mathbb{F}_2^{n+m}\to\mathbb{F}_2$ that vanishes on the graph $\{(x,F(x)) : x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^{n+m}$ (equivalently, the minimum degree of any nonzero annihilator of the indicator of the graph of $F$).

A motivating example is the augmented function associated with a stream cipher: if $S:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is the state-update function and $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ is the filtering function, the augmented function $F_m(x)=(f(x),f(S(x)),\dots,f(S^{m-1}(x)))$ has all of its output coordinate functions linearly equivalent to one another (when $S$ is linear).

Question: Does the existence of pairwise linear equivalences among all output coordinate functions $f_1,\dots,f_m$ of a multi-output Boolean function $F$ influence (constrain, increase, or decrease) the algebraic immunity $\mathrm{AI}(F)$? More precisely, is there a non-trivial bound or structural property relating $\mathrm{AI}(F)$ to the property that $f_1,\dots,f_m$ are all in the same linear-equivalence class?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search turned up follow-up work characterizing algebraic immunity for multi-output Boolean functions (e.g., Armknecht–Krause constructions, IACR ePrint 2012/338) and noting that algebraic immunity is not invariant under affine transformations on the outputs but is invariant under linear transformations on the inputs. However, no source was found that directly resolves whether linear equivalence among all output components of a multi-output function influences its algebraic immunity. The question therefore appears not to have a definitive published resolution.

status_evidence.title: Characterizations on Algebraic Immunity for Multi-Output Boolean Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Several new characterizations of algebraic immunity for multi-output Boolean functions are given, along with related invariants.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work studies algebraic immunity of multi-output Boolean functions but does not directly resolve the influence of linear equivalence between output components.

status_evidence.title: Constructing Single- and Multi-output Boolean Functions with Maximal Algebraic Immunity
status_evidence.snippet: Armknecht and Krause define algebraic immunity for multi-output Boolean functions and study construction of functions with maximal algebraic immunity.
status_evidence.claim: Constructions of multi-output functions with high algebraic immunity have been studied but do not address the linear-equivalence-of-components question.
